stem: A facility wants one amber-trichome percentage to define harvest readiness for every cultivar it grows. Which response best matches the evidence?
choices: Use one calibrated percentage across cultivars because a consistent imaging method should minimize genotype-related maturity differences
Avoid a universal percentage and use repeated representative observations tied to the cultivar and defined production objective
Use a fixed flowering-day threshold instead because calendar age is more comparable across cultivars than trichome development
Use the most mature flower from each crop because leading tissue provides the earliest consistent indication of crop readiness
rationale: Research shows genotype- and age-dependent trichome development and asynchronous maturation. A single universal color percentage should therefore not be treated as a definitive harvest rule across cultivars.
